newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA BUNDLE INDIA OUT FOR 185.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA BUNDLE INDIA OUT FOR 185.

text.p: South Africa's bowlers, led by Alan Donald and aided by their side's superb fielding, bundled India out for 185 runs in the Titan Cup limited-overs triangular series on Tuesday.
South Africa, who have won all their four matches so far, were left needing to score 186 for victory at a comfortable asking rate of 3.72 runs an over.
India, who lost their previous two matches against South Africa in the series, began shakily by losing opener Navjot Sidhu early after electing to bat on what looked a good batting strip.
A brilliant knock of 53 off 69 balls by India's medium pacer Javagal Srinath, promoted to third position on the order, savid India from a worse plight.
Their total of 185 off 48.1 overs is their lowest in the series in which they have won only one match so far.

Indian skipper Sachin Tendulkar, after enjoying an early reprieve when Darryl Cullinan failed to hold a spiralling skier at mid-on, appeared to settle down but was adjudged leg before to Donald to one that came in sharply.

Srinath, hero of India's dramatic victory over Australia at Bangalore, played some fluent strokes and put on 57 runs for the third wicket with Rahul Dravid. He hit four boundaries and hoisted spinner Pat Symcox for a huge six over long-on.
Except for Dravid and Ajay Jadeja, none of the Indian batsmen could last long enough to give any meaningful push to the score.
Donald took three wickets for 31 runs on a strip that offered the bowlers little assistance, followed by Lance Klusener and Nicky Boje who bagged two each.
